messages.content: can read be about yesterday and tomorrow?
yes. the written word read can be used for both. yesterday i read a page is about the past. tomorrow i will read a page is about later.
why do both sentences have the same written word?
some words are written the same way in different sentences. in these examples, yesterday and will help make the time clear. the sound of read is different in the past example.
can you explain the sound with other words?
for the past example, read sounds like red. for the later example, it sounds like the first part of reading.
now give one sentence about what i am doing right now.
i am reading a page now.
change the sentence to my brother.
my brother is reading a page now.
can i say he read a page now?
if you mean what he is doing at this moment, he is reading a page now is the clear choice. he read a page is usually about the past.
only give the yesterday example again.
yesterday i read a page.
now give the tomorrow example, but with two pages.
tomorrow i will read two pages.
my friend made a picture. i like the blue part, but i do not understand what is happening in it. help me say something true and kind.
you could say: i like the color in your picture. would you like to tell me about what is happening in it?
why ask instead of saying the picture has no meaning?
because you do not yet understand it, which is different from knowing that it has no meaning. asking gives your friend a way to explain what they wanted to show.
i only want to say something about the blue part for now.
i like the blue part of your picture.
is that too short?
not if it says what you want to say. a short, true answer can be enough. you do not have to say that you like every part.
what if they ask whether i understand the story in it?
you could say: not yet. i like the blue part, but i would like to hear about the story you are telling.
can i say that without asking them to explain right now?
yes. you could say: i do not understand the whole story yet, but i like the blue part. i would like to hear about it when you want to talk.
only give the first sentence of that message.
i do not understand the whole story yet, but i like the blue part.
write a story about a person leaving a note that is clear to them but not to someone visiting.

a man was waiting for his cousin to visit. he had to go to the shop, so he left a note on the door saying that the key was where he always kept it. when his cousin came, she did not know what place he wanted her to look in. she called him and asked. he told her that the key was in a small container behind the flower near the window. when he returned, he wrote a different note for another person who would visit. this time, he gave the place in words that did not need someone to know the house already.
why did his cousin not understand the first note?
she did not know where he always kept the key. the note needed information he had but she did not.
was the first note useful to nobody?
not for sure. someone who already knew where he kept the key might understand it. the problem was using it for a person who did not know.
write the new note.
the key is in the small container behind the flower near the window.
does that make the note useful to every person in every place?
no. it still needs the person to be at the right house and find the window and flower. clear writing needs enough information that both people know.
can you explain that last sentence with an example?
if there is more than one window with a flower near it, the person may still need to ask which window to use.
finish with the cousin helping him check the new note.
he asked his cousin to read the new note before leaving. she showed him the window and told him where she would look. he knew that the note now gave her enough information.
i had ten coins. i gave four to my sister, then she gave one back. how many do i have?
you have seven coins.
how many of my coins does she still have?
she still has three of your coins.
can you know how many coins she has in all?
no. she may have had coins of her own before you gave her any. we only know that she still has three of the coins you gave her.
now she says she had two coins before. how many does she have?
she has five coins, if she has not given away or used any other coins during that time.
why did you add if?
you gave her starting number and what happened between you. the answer comes from those facts. if other coins came in or went out, the number could be different.
there were no other changes. i now give her two more coins.
then you have five coins, and she has seven.
how many coins do we have together?
you have ten coins and two more together.
why did the number together not change when i gave her more coins?
the coins moved between you, but no coins left the pair of you or came from someone else.
so how many do we have together now?
you still have ten coins and two more together.
i want to ask my sister to read my story. she is busy this week. i do not want her to think she has to do it today.
you could say: would you like to read my story when you have time? there is no need to read it today.
can i say i would like to hear what she thinks too?
yes. you can add that you would like to hear what she thinks, while keeping the time open.
write both parts together.
would you like to read my story when you have time? i would like to hear what you think, but there is no need to read it today.
what if she does not have time this week at all?
you can say that another week is fine if that is true for you. if you need an answer soon, tell her that clearly instead.
i do not need it soon. make that part clear.
would you like to read my story when you have time? i would like to hear what you think, but i do not need an answer this week.
can she say no without giving me a long reason?
yes. asking gives her a choice. she can say that she cannot read it, and you can thank her for telling you.
give me a kind reply if she says she cannot.
thanks for telling me. i understand that you do not have time.
write a story about someone who can remember part of a song from when she was a child. do not write the song itself.

a woman heard a song through an open window and stopped walking for a moment. the first line was like a song her grandfather used to sing. she could remember sitting near him, but not all the words. at home, she asked her brother whether he remembered it too. he knew a different part. they talked about the song without trying to make up the words they could not remember. later, they asked their grandfather, who told them the name. hearing part of it had brought back a memory, even before they knew the whole song.
why did they not make up the parts they could not remember?
they wanted to know the song as their grandfather had known it. making up words could give them a new song rather than the part of the old one they did not remember.
can making up words be fine if they want a new song?
yes, if they want to make their own song and keep clear that it is new. that is a different task from finding the original words.
what did the woman know before asking her brother?
she knew that the line was like a song from when she was a child and that it brought back a memory of her grandfather. she did not know all the words.
make that answer shorter.
she remembered the feeling and part of the song, but not the whole song.
write one question she could ask her grandfather.
do you remember the name of the song you used to sing when we were children?
finish without saying every memory was correct.
he told them the name, and they listened again. some parts were as they remembered, while other parts were different.
give me a short conversation with already and still.
are you still reading the book? no, i have already finished it.
what does still do in the question?
it asks whether the reading is happening up to now. the person asking thinks the reading may not be finished.
what does already do in the answer?
it says that the book is finished by now. in that answer, it also makes clear that the reading is not still happening.
can someone say i have already started but i am still reading?
yes. starting and finishing are different parts. the person can have started before now and be reading now.
make that about dinner.
i have already started eating, but i am still having dinner.
does still having dinner mean someone has had nothing to eat?
no. it says the meal is not finished for them. they may have had some food already.
only give a sentence saying my sister finished her dinner before now.
my sister has already finished her dinner.
now say she has not finished.
my sister is still having dinner.
can the window is closed and the window is open both be true?

if you mean the same window at the same moment, and open and closed are opposite choices, they cannot both be true about it that way. they can be true at a different time, or about a different window.
i mean one window. it was closed in the morning and open after lunch.
then both sentences can be true when you give the time for each: the window was closed in the morning, and it was open after lunch.
can you know who opened it?
no. you gave the change but not the person who made it.
what if i say my father was the only person home then?
that may help you think about what happened, but it is still not the same as him saying he opened it or someone seeing him do it. the window might have been opened before the time you mean.
i saw him open it after lunch.
then you have given the person and the time. you can say: my father opened the window after lunch.
can you keep the morning information too?
the window was closed in the morning. my father opened it after lunch.
why not say it is still open now?
you have not said whether anyone closed it later. the information gives what happened after lunch, not every later moment.
